result: hiPSCs cultured in suspension conditions without microcarriers or ECM components showed increased spontaneous differentiation compared to adherent culture, as evidenced by increased expression of differentiation markers (PAX6, SOX17, T), decreased TRA1-60 expression, and altered gene expression patterns favoring differentiation pathways.
evaluation: All reviewers acknowledged this core finding. Reviewer 1 (sa1) explicitly states 'there is a greater amount of spontaneous differentiation in human pluripotent cells cultured in suspension vs static.' Reviewers 2 (sa2) and 3 (sa3) both describe the finding as 'elegant' and note the authors 'showed elegantly that inhibition of the Wnt and PKC signaling pathways would repress spontaneous differentiation.' No reviewer questioned this fundamental observation.

result: Wnt signaling inhibitors (IWR-1-endo, IWP2) effectively suppress mesendodermal differentiation (SOX17, T expression) in suspension culture, while PKC inhibitors (Gö6983, GF109203X) suppress ectodermal differentiation (PAX6 expression), with combined treatment maintaining pluripotency markers.
evaluation: Reviewers 2 and 3 explicitly support this finding. Reviewer 2 (sa2) states the authors 'showed elegantly that inhibition of the Wnt and PKC signaling pathways would repress spontaneous differentiation into neuroectoderm and mesendoderm in hiPSCs.' Reviewer 3 (sa3) confirms 'the addition of PKCβ and WNT signaling pathway inhibitors to suspension cultures of iPSCs effectively suppresses spontaneous differentiation.' No concerns were raised about these mechanistic findings.

result: PKCα and PKCβ RNA expression and phosphorylated PKCβ protein levels were significantly elevated in suspension conditions compared to adherent conditions, suggesting PKCβ activation contributes to spontaneous differentiation.
evaluation: This mechanistic finding is implicitly supported as part of the overall PKCβ inhibition strategy that all reviewers endorsed. Reviewer 3 (sa3) notes 'the authors have elaborated on the mechanism to some extent-suggesting that PKCβ and WNT signaling pathway inhibition suppresses differentiation,' indicating acceptance of the PKCβ activation data as part of the mechanism.

result: Combined treatment with IWR-1-endo and LY333531 (PKCβ inhibitor) in suspension culture produced homogeneous aggregates, suppressed differentiation markers (PAX6, SOX17, T), maintained pluripotency markers (OCT4, TRA-1-60), and restored cells to a state comparable to adherent culture.
evaluation: All reviewers accepted this key result. Reviewer 2 (sa2) describes it as 'solid study with substantial data to demonstrate the quality of the hiPSC maintained in the suspension culture system.' The editor (sa0) calls it 'a robust, cost-effective method for expanding pluripotent stem cells' and notes the authors 'identified a media condition that maintains iPSCs in suspension cultures by inhibiting the PKCβ and Wnt signaling pathways.' No concerns were raised about these characterization data.

result: Suspension culture with PKCβ and Wnt inhibitors upregulated naïve pluripotency markers (KLF2, KLF4, KLF5, DPPA3) while maintaining OCT4 and NANOG at similar levels to adherent culture, suggesting a shift toward naïve pluripotent states.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 (sa3) explicitly acknowledges this finding, stating 'the authors have elaborated on the mechanism to some extent-suggesting that PKCβ and WNT signaling pathway inhibition suppresses differentiation and shifts cells toward a naïve pluripotency state in suspension cultures.' While noting 'further research is needed to fully understand this process,' the reviewer accepts the data showing this shift.

result: Long-term suspension culture (10 passages) with PKCβ and Wnt inhibitors maintained hiPSC proliferation (~12-fold expansion per passage), uniform aggregate morphology, high OCT4 expression, pluripotency (EB formation), and normal karyotype.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 (sa2) specifically highlights 'long-term maintenance in >10 passages' as part of the 'substantial data to demonstrate the quality of the hiPSC maintained in the suspension culture system.' Reviewer 1 (sa1) describes it as 'a very comprehensive study' with 'a number of unbiased outcomes.' The post-revision comment from Reviewer 2 notes 'new data to further support that suspension culture with Wnt/PKC inhibitors can be used for long-term hiPSC maintenance across multiple cell lines.'

result: The PKCβ and Wnt inhibitor approach was effective across multiple culture media (StemFit, StemScale, mTeSR1), consistently suppressing spontaneous differentiation and maintaining pluripotency markers in suspension conditions.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 (sa2) emphasizes 'robust effect in multiple hiPSC lines' and the post-revision comment specifically mentions 'comparison with current benchmark culture system.' The editor (sa0) notes the importance of 'further testing across more cell lines and in different laboratory settings' for reproducibility, implicitly acknowledging the multi-media data while calling for broader validation.

result: RNA-seq analysis showed that suspension culture with PKCβ and Wnt inhibitors (IWRLY) clustered closely with adherent culture, with upregulation of pluripotency genes (KLF4, ID1) and epithelial markers (CDH1), and downregulation of differentiation transcription factors, while retaining some suspension-specific signatures.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 (sa1) specifically praises 'a number of unbiased outcomes to determine how suspension impacts the behaviour of the cells and in turn how the addition of inhibitors counteracts this effect,' which includes the RNA-seq data. Reviewer 2 (sa2) calls it 'a solid study with substantial data,' implicitly accepting the transcriptomic characterization. No reviewer questioned the RNA-seq findings.

result: Bioreactor culture with PKCβ and Wnt inhibitors at optimized conditions (1-2×10⁵ cells/mL seeding density, 50-150 rpm) maintained hiPSC proliferation, suppressed differentiation markers, preserved pluripotency markers (>90% NANOG/OCT4/SOX2 positive), and maintained normal karyotype over 5 passages.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 (sa1) raised a significant concern about 'the lack of optimization with each bioreactor change,' questioning 'how much of the results the authors observed (e.g. increased spontaneous differentiation) was due to not having an optimized bioreactor protocol in place.' While the post-revision comment states 'The authors did a commendable job in responding and addressing my comments,' this suggests the initial data had limitations that required additional work. Reviewer 2 (sa2) noted 'large-scale expansion of a clinical grade hiPSC using a bioreactor was also demonstrated, which highlighted the translational value,' but this was after revisions.

result: Large-scale bioreactor culture (320 mL) of clinical-grade hiPSCs with PKCβ and Wnt inhibitors achieved ~10-fold expansion in 3-4 days (comparable to adherent culture), produced ~300 stock vials with >90% viability and pluripotency marker expression, maintained normal karyotype, and showed equivalent differentiation capacity to adherent-cultured cells.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 (sa2) specifically highlights this result: 'Notably, large-scale expansion of a clinical grade hiPSC using a bioreactor was also demonstrated, which highlighted the translational value of the findings here.' The editor (sa0) emphasizes the importance for 'high-throughput screens and preclinical studies.' Reviewer 3 (sa3) notes 'This new method of expanding iPSCs has significant potential for clinical applications.' The post-revision acceptance by Reviewer 1 (sa1) suggests concerns about bioreactor optimization were adequately addressed.

result: Single-cell cloning efficiency in suspension culture was improved from <10% (no treatment) to >20% with IWR-1-endo treatment, successfully generating subclones with >3 million cells and high OCT4/TRA1-60 expression by day 28.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 (sa2) notes 'a wide range of applications for the IWR1+LY suspension culture system, including support for freezing/thawing and PBMC-iPSC generation in suspension culture format,' which encompasses single-cell cloning. Reviewer 1 (sa1) states 'the authors were also able to derive new hiPSC lines in suspension with this adapted protocol.' No concerns were raised about the single-cell cloning data.

result: hiPSCs cultured in suspension with IWR-1-endo and LY333531 could be directly cryopreserved and successfully recovered, showing >3 million cells and high OCT4/TRA1-60 expression after thawing across multiple cell lines.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 (sa2) explicitly mentions 'support for freezing/thawing' as one of the 'wide range of applications for the IWR1+LY suspension culture system.' Reviewer 3 (sa3) notes the authors 'can successfully perform single-cell cloning, direct cryopreservation, and iPSC derivation from PBMCs' under these conditions. No reviewer questioned the freeze-thaw data.

result: Reprogramming of PBMCs using SeVdp vectors in suspension culture with PKCβ and Wnt inhibitors successfully generated transgene-free hiPSC lines (bulk and clonal) that maintained pluripotency (EB and teratoma formation), normal karyotype, and showed near-complete SeVdp clearance.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 (sa2) specifically mentions 'PBMC-iPSC generation in suspension culture format' as part of the applications demonstrated. Reviewer 1 (sa1) states 'the authors were also able to derive new hiPSC lines in suspension with this adapted protocol.' Reviewer 3 (sa3) notes 'iPSC derivation from PBMCs' as one of the successful applications. No concerns were raised about the reprogramming data.

result: Reprogramming of PBMCs using episomal plasmid vectors in suspension culture with PKCβ and Wnt inhibitors increased the proportion of TRA-1-60/SSEA4 double-positive cells (78% vs 59% control) and successfully generated clonal hiPSC lines with pluripotency and normal karyotype.
evaluation: This is part of the broader reprogramming results that reviewers accepted. Reviewer 2 (sa2) and Reviewer 3 (sa3) both acknowledged the successful iPSC derivation in suspension culture. The episomal vector approach is an alternative method to SeVdp, and no reviewer distinguished between or questioned either reprogramming method.

result: Treatment with IWR-1-endo and LY333531 for 10 days had no effect on apoptosis in suspension culture, indicating the inhibitors do not compromise cell survival.
evaluation: While not explicitly discussed by reviewers, this safety data supports the overall conclusion that the method maintains cell health. Reviewer 2 (sa2) notes 'a panel of conventional hiPSC QC assays' were performed, which would include viability assessments. The lack of reviewer concern about cell survival or toxicity implicitly supports this finding.
